question: Can a mathematical research-promotion record distinguish a truly independent, exact-subject review from a proposer self-asserting reviewer counts/booleans?
incumbent_gap: MathResearchRecord/FormalizationWitness/NoveltyCertificate use reviewer counts or booleans without content-bound reviewer identity, exact subject binding, procedure identity, or proposer separation.

cases.world: all v1 fields are positive, but proposer_identity_hash equals reviewer_identity_hash for formalization, novelty, and value review
valid review receipt for formal statement A is attached to statement B
novelty review binds the theorem fingerprint but a different literature-manifest hash or cutoff
truth and novelty pass but research-value review has no frozen criteria hash
formalization, novelty, and value reviews bind exact subjects/procedures/worlds and reviewer identity differs from proposer
proof receipt is accepted but the verifier trust receipt is bound to a different proof source or checker manifest

invariants: review identity is content-bound and cannot be replaced by a reviewer count
reviewer identity must differ from proposer identity for a receipt labelled independent
formalization review binds the exact formal statement hash
novelty review binds theorem fingerprint, literature manifest, search procedure and cutoff
value review binds exact formal statement and frozen value-criteria hash
verifier trust binds the exact proof source and checker manifest
the wrapper may narrow incumbent promotion but never silently widen it
all outputs grant no scientific or publication authority by themselves
